title: Galton board: many coin flips make a bell

bodies.name: Funnel
bodies.label: Funnel · releases balls
bodies.describe: Every ball starts in the same place.

bodies.name: Ball
bodies.label: A ball · one random path
bodies.describe: Its final bin is the number of times it bounced right.

bodies.name: Pegs
bodies.label: Pegs · each one a coin flip
bodies.describe: At every peg the ball goes right with probability p.

bodies.name: Bins
bodies.label: Bins · the histogram
bodies.describe: Bin k collects the paths with k right-bounces.

lessons.title: Let the balls fall
lessons.text: Each ball meets one peg per row and goes left or right at random. Watch the bins fill until the bell event.
lessons.explain: A bin count is the number of right-bounces in N independent flips: a binomial distribution, which for many rows is close to a normal curve.

lessons.title: Bias the coin
lessons.text: Make right-bounces likelier. The pile slides right; its centre moves to N·p.
lessons.explain: The mean of a binomial is Np; the spread √(Np(1−p)) also changes.

lessons.title: More rows
lessons.text: Add rows. The board rebuilds; with more flips per ball the bell becomes smoother and wider in bins but narrower relative to N.
lessons.explain: Spread grows like √N while the range grows like N: averages concentrate (the central limit theorem).
